turns.text: hunger arrives as a color before it arrives as an ache — a used-orange throb pulsing behind both eyes, three seconds ahead of the stomach cramp that always follows. something in the wiring crossed over long ago and never uncrossed, ever since the scientists were done with the patch and done with paying for it. paws still, weight low on a rain-slick catwalk bolted under the Research Basement overpass, girders dripping condensate that tastes of solder when it lands on the tongue.

the condensate keeps time better than any clock in this district — drip, drip, drip off a girder stenciled with a warning nobody reads anymore. thirty feet down, the sub-market hums awake: tarps snapping wet, a noodle-cart's burner ticking as it lights, a vendor's radio bleeding half a jingle before it cuts to static. the smell rising up through the grating is fish-fat and ozone and wet concrete, and underneath it, fainter, motor oil from something idling two alleys over that hasn't moved in an hour.

purple. that's what the idling motor sounds like, not a sound at all but a color pressing flat against the inside of the skull, dull and patient, the way it always does right before something bad decides to happen. ears rotate toward it without permission from the rest of the body. the throb behind the eyes sharpens into hunger proper now, plain and stupid, and the catwalk seems to tilt the whole world down toward the noodle-cart's burner glow.

the burner glow catches on wet fur two stalls down — a NekoCorp promo screen bolted above the noodle-cart flickers through its loop, a cartoon cat licking a bowl of SYNTHFISH DELUXE with a jingle that never quite finishes before glitching back to frame one. a patrol drone crosses low between the stalls, rotor wash flattening steam sideways, its belly-light sweeping stall to stall, pausing half a second too long on a stack of unmarked crates near the back wall.

the drone-light passing over pulls something loose that isn't a memory, not really — a kittenhood that was never lived, someone else's warm box and someone else's mother's tongue, filed away in the same drive as everything else and surfacing now for no reason at all. it fades before the light does. what's left is just the crate stack, and the fact that the drone paused on it, and the fact that pausing means something.

the belly-light blinks once, twice, then the drone banks off toward the overpass ramp, its underside speaker crackling to life mid-flight — a bounty tone, tinny and looping, some freelance shanker's silhouette flashed low-res against the crate wall before it's gone: WANTED, LOADING DOCK DISTRICT, APPROACH WITH CAUTION. the vendor at the noodle-cart doesn't even look up. this kind of broadcast is wallpaper down here.

ears flatten anyway, reflex older than understanding. something behind the left one itches, deep, electric, the specific itch of a chip deciding to reboot itself without asking — spiders again, the phantom kind, eight legs of static walking a slow circle around nothing. the crate stack stays a crate stack. hunger wins the argument it's been having with caution, and paws carry the rest of the body down along the drainpipe toward the noodle-cart's blind side.

the drainpipe is warm from something running through it below, a good sign, worth remembering. at the cart's blind side a scrap of batter has slid off the griddle onto the pavement, still steaming, and the vendor's back is turned toward the promo screen, muttering along with a loop he's clearly heard nine thousand times. two stalls over, a fortune-vending machine flickers its one remaining working bulb, dispensing nothing, promising everything.

the batter scrap is gone before it's tasted, swallowed whole, and only after does the burn register — worth it. radio interference climbs up through the back teeth on the exhale, that same crossed-wire trick the brain plays, warning tastes like a struck match even when there's nothing yet to warn about. eyes lift toward the rooftops out of habit, and something up there is very still, and very wrong in the way that stillness always is.

a shape on the ledge four stories up, backlit by a NekoCorp sign so it's mostly silhouette — narrow, deliberate, two flat discs where eyes should catch light instead throwing it back, mirrored, giving nothing away. it doesn't move. it doesn't need to. word travels fast in districts like this about who wears glasses that block the cameras, and why, and the rooftop empties itself of that particular kind of attention exactly when it wants to, not a second sooner.

the mirrored shape is gone by the time the head finishes turning back down — not fled, just elsewhere now, the way certain cats manage to be. the batter-grease taste and the match-taste and the purple hum all layer over each other for a second too long, too much input arriving on the same crossed line, and the only fix is old and reliable: go still, go low, let the noodle-cart's steam hide the shape of a body between two crates.

steam curls around the hiding spot and holds there, thick enough to blur outlines, and for a while the sub-market just runs its own noise without asking anything back — burner tick, tarp snap, the fortune machine's dead bulb flickering its last few volts. rain picks back up somewhere above the overpass, working its way down through six floors of gaps and grating in a slow percussion that has nothing urgent left to say tonight.

one ear stays up even asleep, tuned low, catching the girder-drip counting itself out overhead. somewhere in that count a beat goes missing — not a sound, an absence of one, the kind of gap a paw makes landing soft on wet metal instead of loud. eyes stay shut. the missing beat repeats twice more, patient, unhurried, moving away rather than closer, and that's the only part that matters enough to let the body stay curled instead of bolting.

the missing beats belong to something small working its way along the drainpipe two levels down, unbothered, gone before it was ever really there. the sub-market's last vendor pulls a tarp shut over the noodle-cart and the promo screen finally loops itself dark, one bulb left blinking SYNTHFISH SYNTHFISH SYNTHFISH into an alley with nobody left to sell it to. the rain thins to a drizzle. the district exhales.

the itch behind the ear settles, spiders folding their legs back in, powering down to whatever their idle state actually is. the orange throb behind the eyes has gone quiet too, traded for something duller and heavier, the specific fullness of a stomach that finally has something in it. body curls into the gap between crates, tail wrapped tight, nose tucked, the crossed wires finally agreeing to stop talking over each other for a few hours.

the district settles the way it always does past a certain hour — drones thinning out to their overnight sweep pattern, the noodle-cart's burner ticking down to embers, the promo screen looping its jingle to an audience of nobody. condensate keeps dripping off the same girder, same rhythm, indifferent to who's sleeping under it tonight. somewhere above, the city's glow smears itself thin across the underside of the clouds and stays there.
